simple: Tiny charged particles moving through a material, carrying energy to a lamp or a motor.
analogy: Water moving through the pipes of a house.
precise: The flow of electric charge (in metal wires the charge carriers are electrons) driven by a voltage.
source: D1, D2 of F0-39: Platt, "Make: Electronics"; Horowitz and Hill, "The Art of Electronics" (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: How hard the battery pushes.
analogy: Water pressure.
precise: The electrical potential difference between two points, measured in volts (V).
source: D1 of F0-39 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: How much electricity flows past a point each second.
analogy: How much water flows through the pipe.
precise: The rate of flow of electric charge, measured in amperes (A); 1 mA is one thousandth of an ampere.
source: D1 of F0-39 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: How much something gets in the way of the flow.
analogy: A narrow part of the pipe.
precise: The ratio of voltage to current for a part, measured in ohms (Ω).
source: D1 of F0-39 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A complete loop that electricity can travel around.
analogy: A closed loop of pipe with a pump.
precise: A closed path of conductors and parts through which current can flow from one terminal of a source back to the other.
source: D1 of F0-39 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A store of energy that pushes electricity around a loop.
analogy: A pump that makes pressure.
precise: One or more electrochemical cells that keep a voltage between two terminals, marked + and −.
source: D1 of F0-39 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A rule that links push, flow and narrowness.
analogy: More pressure gives more flow; a narrower pipe gives less flow.
precise: For a resistor, V = I × R, so I = V ÷ R.
source: D1, D2 of F0-39 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A tiny lamp that lights when electricity flows through it the right way.
analogy: A one-way drain that glows when water goes through.
precise: A light-emitting diode: a diode that gives off light when current flows through it in the forward direction.
source: D1, D2 of F0-40 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A part that lets electricity through in one direction only.
analogy: A one-way drain.
precise: A two-terminal part that conducts current mainly from its anode to its cathode and blocks it the other way.
source: D2 of F0-40 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The two legs of an LED: the one for the + side and the one for the − side.
analogy: The top and the bottom of the drain.
precise: The anode is the terminal current enters in the forward direction; the cathode is where it leaves.
source: D2 of F0-40 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A small part that gets in the way of electricity on purpose.
analogy: The water saver that makes the tap narrow.
precise: A part made to have a stated resistance, used here to limit the current through an LED.
source: D1 of F0-40 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The part of the battery's push that the LED needs before it lights.
analogy: The drain needs a little water pressure before it starts to flow.
precise: The voltage across a diode when it conducts in the forward direction; its value comes from the part's datasheet.
source: D2, D3 of F0-40 (D3 = the kit LED's datasheet, not yet chosen) (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The instruction sheet a maker writes for a part, with its true numbers.
analogy: The label on a food packet that says what is inside.
precise: The manufacturer's document that states a part's ratings, limits and behaviour.
source: D3 of F0-40 (kit datasheets, dossier part F, not yet chosen)

simple: A program that pretends to be a real thing so you can try ideas safely.
analogy: Practising a recipe on paper before using the stove.
precise: Software that models a system's behaviour; this course uses its own small C++ text simulators.
source: R1 of F0-40 (lab run in this build)

simple: A tester that measures voltage, current and resistance.
analogy: A pressure gauge you can hold against any part of the pipe.
precise: A measuring instrument with several ranges; in its voltage mode its two probes show the voltage between two points.
source: D1 of F0-40 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A part that opens or closes a gap in a circuit.
analogy: A tap on a pipe (careful: a closed switch lets current through, a closed tap stops water).
precise: A component with contacts that connect (closed) or disconnect (open) a conducting path.
source: D1 of F0-41 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A switch that is on only while you press it.
analogy: A doorbell button.
precise: A momentary switch: a spring returns its contacts to their rest position when released.
source: D1 of F0-41 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Parts placed one after the other in the same loop.
analogy: Two taps on the same pipe: water passes only if both are open.
precise: A connection in which the same current passes through each part in turn.
source: D1 of F0-41 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Parts placed side by side, each giving the current its own path.
analogy: Two pipes side by side: water passes if either tap is open.
precise: A connection in which the parts share the same two connection points, so current can take either path.
source: D1 of F0-41 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A table that lists every combination of inputs and the result.
analogy: A chart on the fridge: if this and that, then ….
precise: A table giving the output of a logic function for every combination of its inputs.
source: D4 of F0-41: Petzold, "Code" (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Change to the other state: on becomes off, off becomes on.
analogy: Pressing the hallway light switch once more.
precise: An operation that inverts a two-state value; here it happens once per new button press.
source: R1 of F0-41 (lab run in this build)

simple: A very small computer on one chip, made to control things like lights and motors.
analogy: A cook who only knows one short recipe card and repeats it all day.
precise: An integrated circuit that contains a processor, memory for the program and data, and input/output pins on one chip.
source: D2 of F0-42 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A little metal leg of the chip that the program can switch on or off, or read.
analogy: A light switch the cook can flip, or a doorbell the cook can listen to.
precise: A terminal connected to the chip's input/output circuits; as a digital output the program drives it high or low, as an input the program reads its level.
source: D2 of F0-42 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: On and off for a pin.
analogy: The light switch up or down.
precise: The two voltage levels of a digital signal; the actual voltages are given in the microcontroller's datasheet.
source: D2, D3 of F0-42 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Steps that repeat again and again.
analogy: Knead, rest, repeat on the recipe card.
precise: A sequence of instructions that the processor carries out again and again; the main loop of a blink program has no end condition.
source: D4 of F0-42: Petzold, "Code" (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A very short time: one second cut into a thousand parts.
analogy: A tiny tick of the kitchen timer.
precise: One thousandth of a second; 1,000 ms = 1 s.
source: Definition; D1 of F0-42 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The program that lives inside a small device.
analogy: The recipe card glued inside the cook's cupboard.
precise: Software stored in a device's non-volatile memory that runs when the device starts.
source: D2 of F0-42 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A part that measures something about the world and turns it into an electrical signal.
analogy: A sense, like eyes or touch.
precise: A device that converts a physical quantity (light, distance, tilt …) into an electrical signal that a circuit or program can read.
source: D1, D2 of F0-43 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: One number the program gets from a sensor at one moment.
analogy: One look at the thermometer.
precise: A single sampled value of a sensor's output, in units stated by its datasheet (or, in the course simulator, made-up units).
source: R1 of F0-43 (lab run in this build)

simple: The line you choose between yes and no.
analogy: If it is darker than this, switch on the hall light.
precise: A chosen value that a reading is compared with to make a two-way decision.
source: R1 of F0-43 (lab run in this build)

simple: Small random wobbles in a sensor's numbers.
analogy: A shaky hand reading a ruler.
precise: Unwanted variation in a measured signal that does not come from the quantity being measured.
source: D2 of F0-43 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Using two lines instead of one, so a decision does not flip back and forth.
analogy: Put a jumper on when it is clearly cold; take it off only when it is clearly warm.
precise: A switching rule with separate turn-on and turn-off thresholds, leaving a dead zone between them.
source: D2 of F0-43 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open); demonstrated by R2 of F0-43

simple: Analog is a number that can take many values; digital here means only two, yes or no.
analogy: A dimmer knob versus a light switch.
precise: An analog signal varies continuously; a digital signal has two levels (high and low). A microcontroller turns an analog voltage into a number with an analog-to-digital converter.
source: D2 of F0-43 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A part that turns electricity into spinning.
analogy: A muscle; or a water wheel.
precise: An electric machine that converts electrical energy into rotation; in a simple DC motor, reversing the current reverses the direction.
source: D1, D2 of F0-44 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A helper circuit that lets a weak signal switch a strong motor current.
analogy: A tap opened by a small control valve.
precise: A circuit (it can be a single chip) that uses a low-current control input to switch the motor's higher current from a separate supply.
source: D2 of F0-44 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: An electronic switch with no moving parts, worked by a small signal.
analogy: A tap opened by a small control valve (registered F1 analogy).
precise: A semiconductor device in which a small current or voltage at one terminal controls a larger current between two others.
source: D2 of F0-44 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Four switches around a motor that let it turn either way.
analogy: Four valves around the water wheel that choose which side the water enters.
precise: A circuit of four switches (in practice transistors) arranged in an H with the motor as the crossbar; closing opposite corners drives current through the motor in one direction or the other.
source: D2 of F0-44 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open); truth model R2 of F0-44

simple: A path that lets current rush from + to − without going through anything useful.
analogy: A burst pipe straight from the tank to the drain.
precise: An unintended low-resistance connection between points at different voltages, which lets a large current flow.
source: D1 of F0-44 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The most current a part may safely give or take.
analogy: The most water a small pipe can carry before it bursts.
precise: A maximum rating stated in the part's datasheet; exceeding it can damage the part.
source: D3 of F0-44 (kit datasheets, not yet chosen)

simple: A robot that drives along a line drawn on the floor.
analogy: Walking along a ribbon while looking at your feet.
precise: A mobile robot whose program uses downward-facing sensors to detect a line and steers to keep the line under its sensors.
source: D2 of F0-45: Lynch and Park, "Modern Robotics" (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Look, decide, act, and do it again.
analogy: Riding a bicycle and correcting your balance (registered F9 analogy).
precise: A repeated cycle that measures the system, compares the measurement with what is wanted, and applies a correction.
source: D1 of F0-45: Åström and Murray, "Feedback Systems" (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Using what you sense now to choose what you do next.
analogy: Looking at the ribbon after every step.
precise: Using a measurement of a system's output to adjust its input.
source: D1 of F0-45 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: How far you are from where you want to be.
analogy: How far the ribbon is from your feet.
precise: The difference between the wanted value and the measured value; not the same as a bug or a compiler error.
source: D1 of F0-45 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A pretend world made of squares, printed as text.
analogy: A floor of square tiles.
precise: A simulation in which positions are whole-number cells of a grid and the robot moves one cell per step.
source: R1 of F0-45 (lab run in this build)

simple: A responsible adult is with you, watching, the whole time.
analogy: An adult staying in the kitchen while the stove is on.
precise: In this university, an adult present for every physical activity at levels L0–L2, able to stop the activity at once.
source: S1 of F0-46: University Authoring Guide, Honesty first and 5.5 (opened in this build)

simple: The electricity in the wall sockets of a building.
analogy: The high-pressure water main under the street, not the garden hose.
precise: The building's alternating-current supply from the electricity network; dangerous, and never used in any lab of this university.
source: S1 of F0-46 (opened in this build); D1 of F0-46 (pending verification; title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A kind of rechargeable battery that can catch fire if mistreated.
analogy: A pressure cooker: useful, but only with strict rules.
precise: A lithium polymer battery; it can catch fire if punctured, over-charged, over-discharged, short-circuited or charged unattended. Not used in F0.
source: S1 of F0-46: University Authoring Guide, Honesty first (opened in this build)

simple: A list you go through, item by item, before you start.
analogy: Checking you have every ingredient before you cook.
precise: A written list of conditions that must all be confirmed before an activity begins.
source: R1 of F0-46 (lab run in this build)

simple: If you are not sure, choose the safe answer.
analogy: If you do not know whether the stove is off, treat it as on.
precise: A design rule: when information is missing or a part fails, the system goes to its safe state.
source: R1 of F0-46 (lab run in this build)
